newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Vitoria hopes to keep cargo growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Vitoria hopes to keep cargo growth in 1997.

text.p: Vitoria airport in northern Spain still expects cargo traffic to more than double this year and hopes it will keep growing at similar levels next year, said Ricardo Gonzalez, the airport's promotor at the provincial chamber of commerce.
"I think if a number of things materialise and there are no problems with air traffic rights we could, if not double again next year, at least come close," he said of traffic volumes.
October was the airport's best month ever for cargo with 2,985 tonnes, taking the total so far this year to 19,765 tonnes compared to 9,109 tonnes in Jan-Oct last year.
"November and December should also be record months and I think we could be close to 30,000 tonnes by the end of the year," Gonzalez said. This compares with 13,782 tonnes in 1995.

The airport at Vitoria, the capital of Spain's Basque Country autonomous region, started handling cargo only two years ago but has developed into a major centre for perishable products and is courier firm DHL's main sorting hub in Spain.

Up to 50 percent of its business is now perishable products, dominated by South African Airways which flies in several freighters a week of fresh fish for the Spanish market and reloads with Spanish fruit and vegetables bound for New York.

Gonzalez said the airport was trying to promote more perishable goods business with Africa and the Far East and also hoped United Parcel Service and TNT would expand their incipient mail business there. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
